notes.title: Journey to the Void: Optimized for Steam Deck!
notes.content:
[p]We've dedicated significant effort to optimizing the game, ensuring a smooth and immersive experience on Valve's portable powerhouse. Get ready to explore the void wherever you go![/p][p][/p][p][i]Journey to the Void[/i] was not merely adapted for Steam Deck; it was designed from the ground up with Valve's handheld platform in mind. Our primary goal is to ensure a fluid, responsive, and above all, enjoyable gaming experience for all players, wherever they may be.[/p][p][/p][p]On-screen glyphs will help you to learn the commands in a couple of fights easily. We were super happy during the playtest to see how easily players got confident with the game![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/649e3d3c516b5cd957f03da95af5358382c1ec59.jpg"][/img][/p][p]With [b]Journey to the Void[/b] on Steam Deck, performance is paramount. You can effortlessly enjoy the game at 60 or even 90 frames per second on the OLED version, ensuring a super smooth experience. [/p][p][/p][p]For those looking to extend battery life, especially during travel, our in-game options allow you to cap the frame rate at 30 FPS, offering significant power savings without sacrificing fun. But to be honest, we run the game at Svilupparty for seven hours at 90 fps without charging the deck![/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Journey to the Void - Demo Update #1
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

We are super excited to share with you the new update of the "Journey to the Void" demo! We have carefully read all your feedback, and we can proudly say that this update is the result of your contribution!

We are a small indie studio, and we really care about making you feel part of the project. So, get ready, because we have listened to your requests and worked hard to implement them!

Here's a short list for those who don't want to go into detail:
[list]
[*] New Card Art
[*] Difficulty Selection
[*] Card Rewards Rework
[*] QOL Updates
[list]
[*] Intention Icons
[*] Tutorial Skip
[*] Deck-specific Fights
[*] Long Press for Controller
[*] Deck Inspector after a Fight
[*] Colored stats in Traits
[/list][*] Game Balancing
[*] Bug Fixes[/list]
If you want to leave feedback, suggest other changes, report a bug, or just engage with the community, pop into our official [url=https://discord.gg/CgPKWTrCz2]discord[/url]!

[h1]New Card Art![/h1]
This is the most visible change made to the demo: we updated all card art, and now each card has its unique artwork! We've heard your feedback, and now cards will be recognizable even from the art alone, without needing to read the name or effects.
Here are a few examples, but many more can be found in the demo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/acae881cc13e15e3e862158ce02ef5eaca2e7b10.png[/img]

[h1]New Feature: Difficulty Selection![/h1]
We gathered a lot of data and listened to all player feedback regarding the demo difficulty. We realized that the game was targeted at a very expert playerbase: the hardcore nature of the game left little to no space for mistakes or distraction, and even one single wrong turn could result in the end of the run.
On one hand, that was the challenging experience we wanted to provide, on the other hand, some players just wanted to enjoy a cute game and the difficulty spike of the first battles was a bit too steep for them. Since we didn’t want to compromise, we decided to do some extra work and implement a difficulty system. From this version of the demo, when creating a new save slot (or starting from scratch), players will be able to select between three difficulties: beginner, normal, and hardcore. 
The beginner difficulty is for those who just want to relax and enjoy the game without worrying too much about strategy and mistakes, the normal difficulty is for players who want a challenge but are not already familiar with the deckbuilding roguelike genre: this mode can be a little more forgiving and allows the player to experiment without being punished. The last difficulty is hardcore: we wanted to preserve the original experience, but now, under this new label, players are warned and will know what they're getting into.
Here is a little preview of how it will be presented in game:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/eb97ecc43a262e12696a84fd6ac489cedc190d04.png[/img]

[h1]System Rework: Card Rewards![/h1]
In previous versions of the demo, at the end of each battle, the player was presented with three individual cards from their card pool. Those cards were always random, and while they did a good job of showcasing the various deckbuilding possibilities, we came up with a more specific method for cards to appear, since we wanted to increase player agency in what they could build in a run.
The most notable improvement is that we have increased the number of slots from 3 to 4, and each slot has specific characteristics on the type of cards that can appear in it. This will allow the player to always have a very wide and varied range of possibilities to choose from.
Each slot will have a specific and varied pool of cards that can appear, so that players are always presented with a meaningful choice.

[h1]QOL[/h1]
In this section, we will show you some improvements we have made to the game in terms of quality of life:
[h3]Intention Icons[/h3]
Following strong requests from many players, we have decided to implement a small icon that displays the monsters' intentions at all times.
This intention represents what the enemy plans to do if nothing changes. However, if during the player's or enemies' turn, the conditions that led to that plan are no longer valid — for example, another enemy moves onto the tile they intended to reach — the intention will be updated accordingly.
For the more experienced players who want a cleaner gaming experience, it is possible to disable the display of this icon in the settings.
[h3]Tutorial Skip[/h3]
When a new profile is created, if there is already at least one in the save files that has completed the tutorial, the option to skip the tutorial and avoid repeating all the explanations will appear, allowing the player to be thrown directly into the first real run.
[h3]Deck-specific Fights[/h3]
We noticed that some early fights presented specific difficulties if the player used a particular deck. We decided to make some fights exclusive to certain decks, so that if a player chooses a particular deck at the beginning of the run, they are not penalized in the early fights by a series of challenging enemies to handle.
[h3]Long Press for Controller[/h3]
We noticed that some players, while using the controller, would occasionally pass their turn accidentally. To solve this problem, we have implemented a light hold on the button to confirm the turn, in order to avoid unintentional presses.
[h3]Deck Inspector after a Fight[/h3]
Some players felt the need to check their deck before choosing a card at the end of a battle. So we added a quick-access system to view the deck more easily.
[h3]Colored stats in Traits[/h3]
When choosing a new character for a run, the traits will have colored text that matches the primary stats color, so that players can easily visualize the stats affected by traits.

[h1]Game Balancing[/h1]
While we have created various difficulties to allow players to experience the game in the way they want, we have still adjusted some values to make the game experience as balanced as possible.
Here is a list of all the changes compared to the previous version of the demo:
[list]
[*] Enemies Balancing:
[list][*] Ghost HP: 5 → 3
[*] Strange Mountain Yeti HP: 25 → 38
[*] Strange Gritty Embermander HP: 21 → 32[/list]
[*] Damage potions are now more effective
[list]
[*] Minor Strength Potion: +1 PD → +3 PD
[*] Medium Strength Potion: +2 PD → + 5 PD
[*] Powerful Strength Potion: +3 PD → + 7 PD
[*] Minor Resonance Potion: +1 ED → +3 ED
[*] Medium Resonance Potion: +2 ED → + 5 ED
[*] Powerful Resonance Potion: +3 ED → + 7 ED[/list]
[*] Cards Balancing:
[list]
[*] Minor Heal → can now be obtained with all three targets.
[*] Full Restore: 30 → 99 (added Not Scalable effect)
[*] Energy Boost → can now be obtained with all three targets.
[*] Clear Mind targets: ⬛⬛⬛ → ⬜⬛⬜ (added Not Scalable effect)
[*] Blizzard effect: Freeze, Not Scalable → Ice Hinder
[*] Blizzard cost: 5 → 4
[*] Blizzard base power: 0 → 6 
[*] Ice Wall effect: Ice Hinder → Freeze, Not Scalable
[*] Ice Wall cost: 3 → 5
[*] Ice Wall base power: 2 → 0 
[*] Flame Cone effect: Flaming → Flaming, Double Damage[/list]
[/list][h1]Bugfix[/h1]
We took the opportunity to fix some bugs: here is a list of the bugs we fixed in this version of the demo:
[list]
[*] Energy and Skill Points usage statistics were wrongly tracked
[*] Some texts were missing for the ice shopper
[*] Fix the wrong card selection with the mouse
[*] The training event appears only for the Villager deck
[*] The postcard stamps now appear only on Boss's death
[*] More readable graphics for wait intention
[*] Fix Italian localization errors
[*] Fix a particular behaviour, quitting the game after the dead scene
[*] Fixed card discard in the tutorial phase
[*] Fixes cards appear on the screen when quitting the run
[*] Fixed the fire boss attack icon
[*] Fixed the wrong Italian enemy description for a monster
[/list]

notes.content:
Hello, players!

notes.title: The Art of Journey to the Void
notes.content:
Hello, players

When designing the world of Journey to the Void, we wanted to create something visually striking, something that would pull players in with its vibrant charm while subtly hinting at the deeper, more complex themes beneath the surface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/7b6ed1415af0ea12cd5bf7fedabceaa26f0f8468.png[/img]

At first glance, the regions you explore are bursting with life: lush landscapes, fascinating creatures, and a dazzling color palette that makes every step of the Journey feel inviting. But as you progress toward the heart of each region, something sinister begins to take hold. Corruption seeps in, twisting the once beautiful environment into something eerie and unsettling. The creatures you once admired become distorted echoes of their former selves, victims of the same chaos you've come to fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/8ce17fbcb54311474492b1adb5ff7bb426ccc369.png[/img]

This stark contrast between the lively, colorful world and the creeping, inescapable decay was a deliberate choice. We wanted players to feel emotionally connected to these regions and see firsthand what's at stake as corruption spreads. Your mission isn't just about survival; it's about reclaiming these worlds, restoring what was lost, and fighting back against the forces that threaten to consume everything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/405522047b12cf488e28b851332bb4de330d6f8a.png[/img]

In Journey to the Void, every step forward is a fight against entropy, a battle to bring light back to a darkening world. This has helped inform the artistic direction of the world as we continue development. 

Until next time, 
RuneHeads

notes.title: Upcoming Features in Journey to the Void
notes.content:
Hello, players

Development on Journey to the Void continues here at RuneHeads, and we wanted to share some of the features we've been working on. 

[b]Traits & Region Fatigue – No Two Runs Are the Same[/b]

Every character will now start a run with randomly assigned Traits—some beneficial, some not so much. This means each playthrough will feel fresh, forcing you to adapt to new challenges (or lucky advantages).

Traits are tied to a new mechanic: Region Fatigue. As you complete runs in a region, the best characters from that area will gradually become unavailable, making it harder to find strong recruits. If you keep hammering the same region, you'll start pulling characters with increasingly difficult (or downright cursed) Traits.

This will be a good reason for most players to explore new regions and keep things balanced. But for those of you who love a brutal challenge—keep going. Think you can complete a run with the most negatively stacked character possible? Either way, it's going to be fun to try!

[b]Track Your Achievements & Show Them Off![/b]

We're also building a detailed stats & achievements tracking system. Players will have access to deep insights on their runs, letting you see just how far you've come (or how many times you've failed spectacularly).

But why keep those achievements to yourself? We're working on a stylish, shareable postcard highlighting your most significant accomplishments. Whether you conquered an impossible run or barely scraped by with a hilariously unlucky character, you can show it off.

These are just the start of the many new features we have planned for Journey to the Void. We can't wait for you all to check them out soon! 

Until then, 
RuneHeads

notes.title: Meet RuneHeads - The Team Behind Journey to the Void
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/280dec6edddf8f35739366a1a76081e17b48e1c1.png[/img]
Hello, players,

At RuneHeads, we're more than just a game studio. We're a team built on education, mentorship, and a shared love for game development. Our founders are teachers at Italian video game academies, and some of our most talented students have joined the team, turning their passion into a career.

Like many developers, we see video games as more than just a pastime. We see them as a valuable tool, a method of self-expression, and something that can bring people together. This is why we started teaching: We wanted to make sure that future generations could get the grounding that wasn't available to us when we were younger. 

There are so many options when it comes to learning how to create games these days, but we still believe learning with a group is essential. Working with others brings new ideas, new ways of thinking, and solutions to problems you would never think of alone. 

This is a key part of how we work at RuneHeads and has gone on to inform the games we make. 

[b]Why Strategy? Why Deckbuilders?[/b]

When deciding on the direction for Journey to the Void, we wanted to create something that played to our strengths. Strategy games have always been at the heart of RuneHeads, and our designers have a long-standing passion for deckbuilders and roguelikes. These genres challenge both players and developers to think critically, adapt, and experiment, something we love doing in both game design and the games we play.

Journey to the Void is the result of that passion. It blends deep strategy with unpredictable roguelike elements to create an experience that's as rewarding as it is challenging. We can't wait for players to dive in and explore everything we've built.

Until next time, 
RuneHeads

notes.title: Looking to the Future of Journey to the Void
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/280dec6edddf8f35739366a1a76081e17b48e1c1.png[/img]
Hello, players,

Development continues on Journey to the Void, and we wanted to share some of the things we're currently working towards. The team is working incredibly hard to shape our vision for the game, so these should give you a glimpse of where we're going on this Journey. 

[b]A Vast, Elemental World[/b]
The full game will feature eight unique elemental regions, each teeming with its own ecosystem of over 100 creatures and 10 epic boss fights. Every elemental power will introduce distinct effects and game-changing combinations, offering multiple ways to experiment and strategize.

[b]The Codex [/b]
Your Journey wouldn't be complete without a way to track your progress. That's where the Codex comes in: A comprehensive almanac that logs every enemy, item, card, and trait you unlock. Think of it as your personal encyclopedia of Journey to the Void's universe.

[b]Your Choices Matter[/b]
Certain special events will force you to make tough moral decisions, permanently shaping the storyline and the fate of the regions you explore. No two journeys will be exactly the same.

[b]Achievements [/b]
Want to push your skills to the limit? The game will feature a wide range of achievements, from easy-to-earn milestones to hardcore challenges that only the most dedicated players will conquer. 

[b]Secrets, Lots of Secrets[/b]
We could tell you about the hidden surprises we're adding, but where's the fun in that? Let's just say that Journey to the Void will reward the most curious and observant players if they know where to look.

This is just a glimpse of what's in store—there's so much more we can't wait to share. Stay tuned, and let us know what you're most excited about in the comments!

Until next time, 
RuneHeads

notes.title: What We Learned from Our First Playtest
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/280dec6edddf8f35739366a1a76081e17b48e1c1.png[/img]
Hello, players!

It's been a little while since we made the first demo for Journey to the Void available. The first thing we want to say is thank you! Thank you to all of you who took the time to try out our game and for all the feedback you've sent our way. We're a small team, so getting this kind of player feedback has been invaluable to us.

One of the big things we learned is how we get players into their first game. We wanted to make this experience as frictionless and easy as possible without overloading the player with a bunch of new systems as soon as they start. 

Game design is full of unexpected challenges, and one of the trickiest we faced was explaining how card direction affects which tiles they hit on the grid. Communicating this sounds simple, right? Well, after playtest feedback and multiple iterations (and a few late-night debates), we finally landed on a solution that feels intuitive and satisfying and we are excited to implement in our next build. 

When adding text to the game, we want to strike a balance between giving players the info they need whilst also not overwhelming them with a textbook's worth of mechanics. One surprising discovery in our playtest? Our discard system went unnoticed. When discarding, players can drag unwanted cards to the bottom left corner. We initially didn’t shout out this feature and relied on a small icon as a hint for this action, it turns out many testers didn't notice it at all! Lesson learned: sometimes, a bigger nudge goes a long way.

These are just two of a bunch of smaller changes and little quality-of-life features we have been adding to Journey to the Void as development continues. The whole demo experience has been invaluable to us, so be sure to keep your eyes peeled here or on our Discord, as we will be running more playtests!

Until next time, 

RuneHeads[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/280dec6edddf8f35739366a1a76081e17b48e1c1.png[/img]

notes.title: A Little About Our World
notes.content:
Hello players, 

Those of you who got to playtest our game will have a sense of what the story of Journey to the Void is about, but if you missed it let us fill you in:

The game is set in a world on the brink of destruction. What was once a peaceful continent is now devastated by the increasingly frequent attacks of corrupted creatures. The player's goal is to unravel the mystery at the heart of the region and restore peace to this world, teetering between life and ruin.

While this is a bleak beginning, there is hope, which is a key element of our game—finding hope and moving forward. Also, seeing how small changes can make a big difference. That and using your deck of cards to defeat enemies!

However, how this story plays out will be up to you with each run you take part in. You are this world’s hero, and you can shape how you want things to go. That choice and agency will meld with the amount of customisation you can bring to your deck and the strategies you employ while playing the game. 

We can’t wait to tell you more and to see you discover how this story can unfold!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/07d7ee90ea6773729c7bcc0a4845991c97047397.png[/img]

RuneHeads

notes.title: Looking ahead to 2025
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/0048f2c840d77705da1ab303b79096dd80509805.png[/img]

Hello players, 

2025 is right around the corner, and we’re incredibly excited for everything that’s going to mean for Journey to the Void! First of all, the game will be launching! We don’t have an exact date for you yet, but it’s going to be in 2025. 

Before that there will be a number of opportunities for you to play the game and give feedback, and we hope to work hand in hand with the community to make the best game we can! Our [url=https://discord.gg/V5HH5DJ8AX ]Discord[/url] server is one of the best places to talk to us directly! We hang out over there a lot, so be sure to join us!

We’ve been working on Journey to the Void for two and a half years now and it’s been such a joy for us. From sketching the very first prototype to exhibiting it for the first time at Milan Games Week. Then we had our first public playtest (thank you again), and on both occasions, we learned so much from watching people play our game for the first time. 

It’s a little scary to put your work out there, you hope it connects with people but you also hope it just works! We feel incredibly thankful that people have enjoyed it and want to follow what we’re doing. 

So, what does 2025 look like for us here at RuneHeads? Well, it’s going to be a lot of work, but we wouldn’t want to be doing anything else!

We can’t wait to share this journey with you!

RuneHeads

notes.title: Journey to the Void playtest starts now!
notes.content:
Hello players,

From now [b]until 18th December[/b] we’re running a Journey to the Void playtest. This is the first chance to play the game we’re opening up for the public apart fom a small audience at Milan Games Week last month. We’re so excited to hear feedback on everything, from card balance to core gameplay mechanics but we’re especially looking for feedback on how the game onboards new players. 

There are a few ways in the game of building your character (some more effective than others in this particular experience) and a final boss for you to face down against. Let us know in the Discord if you find the journey enjoyable, any suggestions and bugs you may come across and whether you manage to defeat the boss! 

We just want to reiterate that this is our [b]first playtest, and not a demo[/b], so please be aware that content may change between now and launch but we’re really looking forward to gathering feedback on the game!

Where can you give us feedback I hear you ask? We’re glad to open the doors to our Discord which you can find [b][url=https://discord.gg/V5HH5DJ8AX]here[/url][/b]. You’ll find spaces to speak with the devs, report bugs, leave feedback and discuss Journey to the Void in more detail. 

[h3]HOW TO JOIN THE PLAYTESTS:[/h3]
Go to the Journey to the Void Steam page
Hit the Join Playtest Button (you'll need to be logged in)
Please wait for us to accept you (We’ll check regularly so please be patient)

We hope you enjoy the playtest and we thank you in advance for your support!

Thank you,

notes.title: Journey to the Void Announced!
notes.content:
Last week we launched the Steam page for [b]Journey to the Void[/b]! Combining a turn-based strategy RPG with a roguelite deck-builder, each run will feature challenging battles and a story that changes based on your choices. We’re so excited to have the game out there but now we need your help! 

[h3]Features[/h3]
We’re still in the middle of development for Journey to the Void but we wanted to run through some of our targeted features for the full game when we launch next year:
[list]
[*] 25 different arenas (8 elemental regions) - Completing arenas and challenges will unlock player backgrounds that modify your starting deck
[*] 100+ different cards, items and weapons with thousands of unique effect combinations
[*] 100+ events - Linked events that create an immersive storytelling across the different runs
[*] 100+ different enemies and 10 unique boss fights
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/258d99398b887f2b4e5cd43fde7ca3ace456d5d3.jpg[/img]
[h3]Playtests[/h3]
We’ll be setting up playtests for us to gather useful feedback in the near future for people who couldn't make Milan this weekend. Please keep an eye out for our Steam announcements and on our social channels for when we start our search for playtesters!

[h3]Milan Games Week[/h3]
We went to Milan Games Week this weekend for people to get their first hands-on of the game. We had a demo for people to jump into, merch to hand out and a lot of space for feedback on the game which went to full use! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45308526/72d171ebed14c404fef771da38133e42b18c73c0.jpg[/img]
[h3]The Start of the Journey! [/h3]
Finally, thank you if you’ve read all of this and joined us at the start of this Journey (to the Void)! We’ve got big plans and high hopes for next year and we can’t wait to start gathering feedback, closing on our vision for the game and building a community of heroes who will join us in venturing into the darkness. Please spread the word, wishlist the game and follow the page - it makes a bigger difference than you may realise. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3210490/Journey_to_the_Void/
